title: Qwen3 Technical Report
data_curation: Pre-training uses 36T tokens across 119 languages (up from 29 in Qwen2.5), spanning coding, STEM, reasoning, books, multilingual text, and synthetic data. To expand the corpus, Qwen2.5-VL extracts text from PDFs (refined by Qwen2.5), and Qwen2.5/Qwen2.5-Math/Qwen2.5-Coder synthesize trillions of tokens (textbooks, QA, instructions, code). A multilingual annotation system labels 30T+ tokens by educational value, field, domain, and safety; unlike prior source/domain-level mixing, the mixture is optimized at instance level via small proxy-model ablations. For post-training, the Long-CoT cold-start set (math, code, logic, STEM) is query-filtered with Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (removing unverifiable/easy items) and response-generated with QwQ-32B; 3,995 query-verifier pairs are collected for Reasoning RL. Stage-3 SFT fuses rejection-sampled thinking data with curated non-thinking data (coding, math, instruction-following, multilingual, creative writing, QA, role-playing), with extra translation tasks for low-resource languages.
curriculum: Pre-training is three stages: S1 General (30T+ tokens, seq len 4096, language/knowledge); S2 Reasoning (5T higher-quality tokens, more STEM/coding/synthetic, accelerated LR decay); Long-Context (hundreds of billions tokens at 32768, 75% of text 16K-32K and 25% 4K-16K, using ABF RoPE plus YARN/DCA for 4x inference length). Post-training for flagship models (235B-A22B, 32B) is four stages: (1) Long-CoT cold-start SFT, (2) Reasoning RL via GRPO, (3) Thinking Mode Fusion via continual SFT, (4) General RL. The first two build thinking; the last two add non-thinking and broad alignment. Lightweight models skip this and use Strong-to-Weak Distillation (off-policy then on-policy logit distillation) at ~1/10 the GPU hours, with better pass@1/pass@64.
method: The core contribution is a single model integrating thinking and non-thinking modes via a chat template with /think and /no_think flags and an empty thinking block for non-thinking samples, plus a thinking-budget mechanism that halts reasoning at a user threshold and injects a stop-thinking instruction. Reasoning RL uses GRPO with large batches, many rollouts per query, off-policy sampling for sample efficiency, and entropy control (kept steady/increasing) for stable training. General RL covers 20+ tasks (instruction/format following, preference alignment, agent tool-use with real environment feedback, RAG) using three reward types: rule-based, model-based scoring against a reference answer (Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct), and a trained reference-free reward model. Strong-to-Weak Distillation first does off-policy logit distillation from teacher /think and /no_think outputs, then on-policy distillation where the student samples and is fine-tuned by minimizing KL divergence to teacher (Qwen3-32B or 235B-A22B) logits.
eval_metrics: Base models: MMLU, MMLU-Pro, MMLU-redux, BBH, SuperGPQA, GPQA, GSM8K, MATH, EvalPlus (HumanEval/MBPP/+), MultiPL-E, CRUX-O, MGSM, MMMLU, INCLUDE. Post-trained: MMLU-Redux, GPQA-Diamond (10x avg), C-Eval, LiveBench, IFEval (strict), Arena-Hard, AlignBench, Creative Writing v3, WritingBench, MATH-500, AIME'24/'25 (64x avg of 30 Qs), ZebraLogic, AutoLogi, BFCL v3, LiveCodeBench v5, CodeForces Elo, Multi-IF, MT-AIME2024, PolyMath, MLogiQA, RULER; in-house CounterFactQA, LengthCtrl, ThinkFollow, ToolUse. Thinking mode uses temp 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20; non-thinking temp 0.7, top-p 0.8.
key_results: Qwen3-235B-A22B (Thinking) scores 85.7 AIME'24, 81.5 AIME'25, 70.7 LiveCodeBench v5, 2056 CodeForces rating, 70.8 BFCL v3, outperforming DeepSeek-R1 on 17/23 benchmarks with 60% activated params; its AIME'24 rose 70.1->85.1 over 170 RL steps. On-policy distillation beats RL on Qwen3-8B (74.4 vs 67.6 AIME'24) at ~1/10 the GPU hours (1,800 vs 17,920) and lifts pass@64.
evolution_note: Qwen3 builds on Qwen2.5 and the 2024-2025 reasoning-model wave (o1, DeepSeek-R1, QwQ), reacting to the cost of switching between separate chat and reasoning models by unifying both modes with a controllable thinking budget. Its Strong-to-Weak distillation and unified-mode design motivate later efficient small-model reasoning and agent-RL research focused on inference-time scaling.
